intervals.label: data taking with the detector under construction
intervals.note: Supermodules were added in turn; the quote gives March 1989 to April 1994 with the detector under construction. The mid-1994 start of the full-detector interval follows.
intervals.quote: Data were taken from March 1989 till april 1994 with the detector under construction and from the middle of 1994 till the end of 2000 with the full detector.

intervals.label: data taking with the full detector
intervals.note: Start 'the middle of 1994' (month precision, approximate). End: 'running until December 2000' (arXiv:hep-ex/0612057, §1) and 'to the end of year 2000' (arXiv:hep-ex/0210006).
intervals.quote: Data were taken from March 1989 till april 1994 with the detector under construction and from the middle of 1994 till the end of 2000 with the full detector.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: Terminal event: end of data taking, December 2000.
intervals.quote: The detector started data taking in 1989 and it was running until December 2000.

placements.note: Hall B is stated by the MACRO papers; the site point is the shared campus-grade LNGS point (no hall coordinate published). Start is the first data taking (March 1989, detector under construction).
placements.quote: The detector was located in Hall B of the underground Gran Sasso Laboratory (Italy).

length.quote: The full detector had global dimensions of 76.5 × 12 × 9.3 m3

summary.plain: A long, low building-sized array of scintillator tanks, streamer tubes and track-etch plastic that recorded muons crossing the Gran Sasso rock, 1989 to 2000.
summary.technical: Modular detector of supermodules (each 12.6 x 12 x 9.3 m^3) combining liquid scintillation counters, limited streamer tubes and nuclear-track detectors, with a rock absorber; global size 76.5 x 12 x 9.3 m^3.

technology.quote: three sub-detectors: liquid scintillation counters, limited streamer tubes and nuclear track detectors
technology.value: Three sub-detectors in a modular (supermodule) structure: liquid-scintillator counters, limited streamer tubes and nuclear-track detectors, plus a rock absorber
